error_categories.name: Ignoring Previous Results/Handoffs
error_categories.description: Agent ignores or contradicts data, results, or instructions from previous agents or managers, proceeding with invalid assumptions.

error_categories.name: Hallucinating/Inventing Data
error_categories.description: Agent creates fictional data, results, or handoffs that don't exist or contradict actual information.

error_categories.name: Plan/Instruction Deviation
error_categories.description: Agent fails to follow specific steps, roles, or coordination plans defined by managers or orchestrators.

error_categories.name: Repetitive Failure Loops
error_categories.description: Agent repeatedly attempts same failed approach despite clear errors or instructions to change strategy.

error_categories.name: Context Corruption
error_categories.description: Agent introduces incorrect information that corrupts the shared context for subsequent agents.

source_comparison: Algo_Generated errors predominantly involve ignoring previous results/handoffs (65%), suggesting algorithmic agents struggle with maintaining context and respecting dependencies. Hand_Crafted errors show more balanced distribution with higher rates of hallucination (35%) and plan deviation (30%), indicating human-designed failures target more sophisticated coordination breakdowns and creative failures. Hand-crafted cases also feature more repetitive failure loops (8% vs 3%), suggesting intentional stress-testing of recovery mechanisms.
actionable_insights: Fix context propagation and handoff validation first, as 'Ignoring Previous Results' is the most prevalent failure (affecting 65% of algorithmic errors). Implement stronger dependency tracking and validation checks before agents proceed with actions. This would address the core coordination failure affecting both automated and hand-crafted scenarios.
